required_patterns.json-schema-validation: All Bible data must conform to JSON Schema Draft-07 definitions. Schemas define strict structures with $ref references between related schemas.
required_patterns.content-schema-recursion: The content-schema.json uses recursive $ref to allow arbitrarily nested content structures (strings, objects, or arrays of content).
required_patterns.book-identifiers: Books use 3-character uppercase identifiers (e.g., 'GEN', 'MAT', 'REV') that must match entries in bible-books.json.
required_patterns.version-book-ordering: Each Bible version maintains its own book ordering via the 'order' property (1-indexed, sequential, no gaps).
required_patterns.ajv-validation: Use AJV library for JSON Schema validation with support for $ref resolution across schema files.
required_patterns.atomic-file-writes: Write JSON output via writeJsonFile() and raw text (Markdown, pre-formatted JSON) via writeFileAtomic(), both from functions/writeJsonFile.ts. Do not call fs.writeFileSync directly for pipeline output — both helpers stage bytes to a temp file and rename over the target, retrying on a backoff if the rename is transiently blocked.
required_patterns.json-canonicalization-from-parsed-data: Any JSON formatting pass (writeJsonFile()'s formatJsonData(), and validate.ts's own reformat-on-change check) must derive its output from JSON.parse'd data, never from a file's existing raw text. Prettier preserves whichever line breaks its input already has rather than re-deciding them from width, so formatting raw text lets a stray break (e.g. from a prior bug, or a different tool's output style) persist across every future validate run instead of self-correcting.
required_patterns.cross-chapter-bible-link-splitting: A bibleLink target whose range spans two chapters of the same book (e.g. '2 Kings 6:31–7:20') must be split into two chapter-scoped links joined by a literal en dash. Enforced by utils/crossChapterLinks.ts and audited corpus-wide by utils/auditCrossChapterLinks.ts.
required_patterns.strong-node-text-flow-conventions: A joining space belongs on the leading edge of the node it joins, never the trailing edge of the node before it; a connector word left unmerged should fold forward into the strong-carrying neighbor after it, never backward; a verse's own outermost content must never open with whitespace. Audited (read-only, no --fix) by utils/auditStrongsNodes.ts across five distinct drift shapes.
required_patterns.no-meaningless-content-nodes: A node must never carry only formatting (marks/script) with no text to apply it to, nor an empty '' text husk left over from stripped marks. Enforced by utils/validate.ts's findMeaninglessContentNodes().

architectural_constraints.no-database: All data stored as flat JSON files, no traditional database. Read/write via Node.js fs module.
architectural_constraints.schema-reference-urls: Schema $id and $ref use GitHub URLs but resolve locally via AJV schema registration.
architectural_constraints.immutable-source-data: Bible verse JSON files in version directories are source data; exports go to separate exports/ directory.
architectural_constraints.content-flexibility: Content can be plain string, structured object with metadata, or array combining both. Code must handle all cases.
architectural_constraints.content-nested-carries-marks: A ContentNested wrapper ({content, strong, ...}) may itself carry marks (bold/italic/woc/small-caps applying to an entire nested subtree), not just leaf ContentObject nodes.
architectural_constraints.strong-number-format: Strong's numbers must match pattern '^[GH][0-9]{1,4}$' (G for Greek, H for Hebrew).
architectural_constraints.version-scoped-chapter-lengths: A chapter's last verse must be read from that version's own verse records, never a shared or borrowed table — versification (e.g. Romans 14's last verse) differs between translations.
architectural_constraints.single-footnote-per-node: The schema allows only one foot per node; a word's second footnote must ride as a textless sibling node immediately after it, carrying only foot.

required_patterns.react-hooks: Use React 18 hooks (useState, useEffect, useMemo, useRef) for all state and lifecycle management.
required_patterns.babel-in-browser: JSX transpiled at runtime via Babel standalone. No build step for frontend.
required_patterns.cdn-dependencies: React, ReactDOM, Tailwind CSS, Font Awesome, and fonts loaded via CDN in index.html.
required_patterns.component-registration: Each component file assigns to window object (e.g., 'window.App = App') for cross-file access.
required_patterns.tailwind-utility-classes: Use Tailwind CSS utility classes for styling. Dark mode via 'dark:' prefix variants.
required_patterns.script-specific-fonts: Hebrew text uses 'David Libre' font with RTL direction; Greek uses 'EB Garamond'; Latin uses 'Atkinson Hyperlegible'.
required_patterns.shared-footnote-text-extraction: Footnote display text must be derived through the single shared window.getFootnoteText (web/public/js/footnoteText.js), not re-flattened inline per rendering path — it recurses through every foot.content shape (string, array, {bibleLink, content?}, {text}) so every footnote flattens identically regardless of which node shape it's attached to.

architectural_constraints.no-build-process: Frontend has no webpack/vite/rollup. All JS loaded directly via script tags with Babel transpilation.
architectural_constraints.single-page-app: Single index.html entry point. All navigation is in-memory state changes.
architectural_constraints.prop-drilling: State flows from App component down via props. No Context API or global state.
architectural_constraints.component-order: Script tags in index.html must load in dependency order (Icons → Toggle → ... → App); footnoteText.js must load before ContentNode.js, since it's a window-global dependency, not a module import.
architectural_constraints.dark-mode-class: Dark mode toggled via 'dark' class on document.documentElement.

required_patterns.static-public-dir: Static files served from 'web/public/' directory. Root '/' serves index.html.
required_patterns.content-endpoint-pattern: Bible content fetched via '/api/content/{versionId}/{bookId}' returning array of verse objects.

architectural_constraints.no-spa-routing: No client-side routing library. Navigation is state-based within single page.
architectural_constraints.no-framework-server: Simple Node.js http server without Express or other frameworks.
architectural_constraints.directory-traversal-prevention: Server checks that resolved file paths start with PUBLIC_DIR to prevent traversal attacks.
architectural_constraints.mime-type-mapping: Server maps file extensions to MIME types for proper content-type headers.

required_patterns.centralized-app-state: All application state lives in App component: versions, selections, content, settings, UI state.
required_patterns.derived-state-memoization: Use useMemo for computed values (currentVersion, availableBooks, currentBook, chapterContent).
required_patterns.settings-object: Settings stored as single object with keys for all display options (paragraphMode, showStrongs, darkMode, etc.).
required_patterns.toggle-pattern: Boolean settings toggled via toggleSetting function that spreads previous state.

architectural_constraints.no-persistence: Settings and state not persisted to localStorage. Reset on page reload.
architectural_constraints.no-async-state: No async state management (no React Query, SWR). Simple fetch in useEffect.
architectural_constraints.loading-state: Loading boolean tracks API request state; content cleared on error.

required_patterns.dual-export-formats: Export to both text-vbv-strongs (annotated text) and markdown-par (paragraph markdown).
required_patterns.recursive-content-processing: Content processing functions must handle string, object, and array recursively.
required_patterns.footnote-lettering: Footnotes labeled with letters (a, b, c...) cycling after 'z', per chapter.
required_patterns.chapter-grouping: Markdown export groups verses by chapter with ## headers.
required_patterns.shared-emphasis-delimiter-spans: Adjacent array siblings carrying the same open bold/italic (b/i) marks must render under one shared open/close delimiter pair, not one pair per sibling — tracked as an open/close transition between consecutive items, not per-item wrapping. Per-item wrapping produces broken markdown like '**word****word**' instead of '**word word**'.

architectural_constraints.version-directory-mirroring: Export directories mirror version directory structure.
architectural_constraints.cli-arguments: Export script accepts optional version and bookId arguments for selective export.
architectural_constraints.main-module-check: Export only runs when script is main module (require.main === module).
